texts.li: {A_nameDef} sat up with {B_nameDef} through the worst night of the illness, changing the cloth on {B_possessive} forehead every hour.
{A_nameDef} slept in a chair by {B_nameDef}'s bed night after night and wouldn't hear of anyone else taking a turn.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the same few stories over and over through the sick days, because {B_nameDef} kept asking.
When {B_nameDef}'s illness was at its worst, {A_nameDef} held {B_possessive} hand and talked about nothing until morning.
{A_nameDef} stuck a candle in a heel of bread for {B_nameDef}, to mark {B_possessive} first days back on {B_possessive} feet.
{A_nameDef} carved {B_nameDef} a walking stick for the weak days, with {B_nameDef}'s name cut into the handle.
{A_nameDef} kept to {B_nameDef}'s slow new pace without once hurrying {B_objective}.
{A_nameDef} has been saving {B_nameDef} the best of every meal to build {B_objective} back up, and won't take no for an answer.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: who gave it to whom

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have come down with the same thing and are arguing over who gave it to whom.
{A_nameDef} said {B_nameDef} had brought it in, and {B_nameDef} said {A_nameDef} had had it first.
Comparing symptoms, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} each claimed to have it worse.
{A_nameDef} blamed {B_nameDef}'s dirty cup for what was going round, and {B_nameDef} blamed {A_nameDef}'s dirty everything.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: argued about who made whom ill

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: an evening at the camp

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} came back from the strangers' camp full of stories and someone else's stew.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} learned a song at the camp and sang it badly all the way back.
{A_nameDef} took {B_nameDef} to meet a family at the camp who had walked all the way from the coast.
At the camp, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} learned a game played with stones on a board and lost every round.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: an evening at the camp together

texts.li: {A_nameDef} saw {B_nameDef} slip something to the strangers at the camp and demanded to know what, and why.
{A_nameDef} accused {B_nameDef} of spending more time at the camp than at work, and {B_nameDef} said the company there was better.
{A_nameDef} counted the stores twice and then looked hard at {B_nameDef}, who has been friendly with the camp.
{A_nameDef} missed the council meeting and blamed {B_nameDef}, who was there, for how it went.
{A_nameDef} cornered {B_nameDef} after the council had met and wanted to know why {B_pronoun} hadn't spoken up for {A_objective}.
{A_nameDef} heard from {B_nameDef} what the council had decided while {A_pronoun} was away, and took it out on the messenger.
On the same side at the council, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} kept making their case to each other long after it was over.
{B_nameDef} had backed {A_nameDef}'s point at the council, out loud, and {A_nameDef} came over to say thanks.
With the council over, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} put their heads together over how to win the next vote.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: fears in the night

texts.li: {A_nameDef} woke {B_nameDef} in the night, shaking from a fear {A_pronoun} couldn't name, and {B_nameDef} sat up with {A_objective} until dawn.
{A_nameDef} admitted to {B_nameDef} that {A_pronoun} sleeps with a weapon close by, and {B_nameDef} admitted that {B_pronoun} does too.
{B_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} awake in the dark, listening to every sound, and stayed until {A_nameDef} fell asleep.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what frightens {A_objective} most, and {B_nameDef} didn't laugh.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: {B_nameDef} sat up with {A_nameDef} through a frightened night

texts.li: {B_nameDef} let {A_nameDef} talk about the one {A_pronoun} had lost for as long as {A_pronoun} needed, and didn't hurry {A_objective}.
{B_nameDef} sat with {A_nameDef}, saying nothing, until {A_nameDef} was ready to get up again.
{B_nameDef} took over {A_nameDef}'s chores so that {A_nameDef} could grieve in peace.
{B_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} a warm drink and a funny old story, and {A_nameDef} laughed in spite of everything.
{A_nameDef} finally told {B_nameDef} what {A_pronoun} thinks of {B_objective}, at the top of {A_possessive} voice.
{A_nameDef} laid out every grievance {A_pronoun} had with {B_nameDef}, in order, starting from the first.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} exactly what {B_pronoun} could do with {B_possessive} opinions, and {B_nameDef} shouted right back.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} had it out at last, loudly, and settled nothing.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a peace offering

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came to ask {B_nameDef}'s advice on a job {A_pronoun} already knew how to do, which was {A_possessive} way of making up.
After their argument, {A_nameDef} saved {B_nameDef} the best piece of the next meal.
{A_nameDef} found {B_nameDef} after their spat and said sorry, plainly, which was harder than {A_pronoun} had expected.
{A_nameDef} mended the thing of {B_nameDef}'s that had started the argument, and left it where {B_nameDef} would find it.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a peace offering after a quarrel

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} found they missed the same things about home, down to the sound of rain on a proper roof.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} traded songs from home and sang them both until someone asked them to stop.
{A_nameDef} walked {B_nameDef} through {A_possessive} old home in words, room by room, and then listened to {B_possessive}.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} described the food from home to each other until both of them were hungry.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: something for the hungry

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} agreed to set aside part of their own rations for the hungry towns.
{A_nameDef} talked {B_nameDef} into giving up a meal a week for the towns, then gave up two.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued over the right way to pack food for the hungry towns.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: put something by for the hungry

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: news of the sick

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the sickness in the towns, who they knew there, and whether it would come here.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} made each other promise to wash before every meal until the sickness out there has passed.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whether {B_pronoun} had family in the towns, and {B_nameDef} took a long time to answer.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: worried together about the sickness in the towns
